newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, more downside seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, more downside seen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Monday after failing to extend gains inspired by the dollar's rise to a 50-month high.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract lost 190 points to end at 17,690 on low volume of 13,275 lots.
The dollar was quoted at 124.53/58 yen at 0750 GMT after hitting a high of 125.00 yen earlier in Tokyo.
Weakness in construction and banking sector shares dragged the Nikkei average down 144.92 points to close at 17,715.67.
"With the close below 17,800, I think we should try lower. The immediate support is at 17,550-17,600 but that might not hold," said a trader with a local institution.

He said the Nikkei cash market was likely to see some bargain hunting interest around the 17,500 level but the futures market was still in the process of building a base and could head back to the low just under 17,000, seen earlier this year.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 350.6 against an opening 346.7 on volume of 2,071 lots.

Taiwan stocks surged 150.13 points to close at 8,517.70 on bullish sentiment after last week's announcement that Taipei would raise bank shareholding limits from July, a move that could attract up to T$47 billion in additional funds to the market.
News that Taiwan's Consumer Price Index rose a lower than expected 1.09 percent in March, the slowest rise in years, also supported the market, Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary.
"The release of these figures will give the central bank little reason to raise rates," it said.
